1. Executive intent
 Today: Peak_Trade already has strong separation between research, validation, risk/safety, runtime evidence
 and controlled promotion. However, a fully proven automated closed learning loop from runtime incidents to
validated candidate changes must not be assumed.
 Future: every material system decision becomes a versioned evidence object with context, reason codes,
 expected outcome, realized outcome, counterfactual evaluation and a deterministic lineage.
 Safety invariant: KillSwitch, stale-data guards, reconciliation blocks and hard risk limits remain independent
 authorities. A learner may analyze them; it may never override them in the same runtime decision.
 Learning invariant: runtime observations create evidence and hypotheses - never silent self-modification.
 
 Promotion invariant: candidate changes re-enter Research -> Replay/Backtest -> Walk-Forward -> Monte Carlo
 -> Stress -> Safety Regression -> Shadow/Testnet -> explicitly authorized promotion.

4. Canonical Decision Event
The central future primitive should not be a trade. It should be a Decision Event. A trade is only one possible
outcome. NO_ENTRY, NO_EXIT, BULL_TO_BEAR, BEAR_TO_BULL, STALE_BLOCK, RISK_BLOCK,
KILL_SWITCH and RECONCILIATION_BLOCK are equally first-class decisions.
DECISION_EVENT event_id / correlation_id event_time_utc decision_type decision_result reason_codes[]
hard_block_reasons[] market_snapshot_ref feature_snapshot_ref bull_bear_state_before / after
dynamic_scope_ref data_quality_ref risk_snapshot_ref position_snapshot_ref execution_snapshot_ref
code_sha / config_hash / model_version expected_outcome_ref authority_owner evidence_hash
Required property: given the same immutable inputs, versions and policy, the evaluator must
reproduce the same classification. Any stochastic model must persist seed, model artifact/version and
exact feature vector.
5. KillSwitch learning loop
Runtime behavior and learning behavior are intentionally decoupled.
T0: anomaly / safety condition | v KILL SWITCH AUTHORITY ---> fail-closed protective action | v
immutable incident evidence | v post-event attribution | +--> trigger correctness +--> root cause
+--> consequence avoided / incurred +--> counterfactual paths | v learning hypothesis | v offline
validation + safety regression | v promotion candidate (never automatic live override)
Suggested KillSwitch classification
Class
Meaning
TRUE_POSITIVE
A real protected condition existed and the switch reacted as specified.
FALSE_POSITIVE
The switch fired although the protected condition was not actually present or was misattributed.
FALSE_NEGATIVE
A protected condition existed but the switch did not fire or fired too late.
TRUE_NEGATIVE
No protected condition and no trigger.
TIMING_LABEL
TOO_EARLY / ACCEPTABLE / TOO_LATE, evaluated separately from profitability.
Critical rule: profitability after the event is not the ground truth for safety correctness. A KillSwitch can
be correct even if the market subsequently moves favorably. The evaluation target is whether the
safety contract was satisfied under information available at decision time.
6. Stale-data, Bull/Bear and Dynamic-Scope learning
Staleness is an information-quality condition, not a market direction. Dynamic Scope and Bull/Bear state should
consume trusted/fresh inputs; a stale guard can freeze or block a decision surface without inventing a market-state
conclusion.
trusted + fresh observation | v Dynamic Scope / Bull-Bear evaluation | v state transition OR
deliberate non-transition stale / untrusted observation | v STALE_BLOCK | +--> preserve last
admissible state as policy defines +--> prevent untrusted scope/state mutation +--> emit incident
evidence
Post-event attribution should distinguish at least: venue feed delay, network delay, local consumer backlog,
timestamp defect, clock skew, missing observation, parser/schema defect and internal processing latency. This
prevents the system from 'learning' a looser freshness threshold when the actual defect is infrastructure.
7. Outcome and counterfactual evaluation

Every material decision should later receive an Outcome Record. The record must preserve two truths: what
actually happened and what can legitimately be inferred about alternatives. Counterfactuals must therefore
carry confidence and admissibility labels rather than pretending that unobserved alternatives are facts.

Purpose

OBSERVED / REPLAYABLE / MODELLED / UNAVAILABLE.

Did the safety contract behave correctly?

Did the trading/state decision behave as intended?

8. Learning without unsafe online self-modification
EVENT -> immutable evidence -> deterministic attribution -> outcome/counterfactual labeling ->
aggregate cohort analysis -> hypothesis -> candidate change -> deterministic replay -> backtest ->
walk-forward -> Monte Carlo -> stress / fault injection -> safety regression suite -> shadow ->
testnet (when authorized) -> explicit promotion gate -> live (when separately authorized) ->
monitoring / rollback
 No learner edits live thresholds, KillSwitch semantics or risk limits directly.
 
 No candidate is promoted solely because it improves PnL; safety and robustness constraints remain hard gates.
 
 All candidate comparisons use versioned datasets/configs/code and retain rejected candidates.
 
 Promotion requires explicit evidence that the candidate does not degrade safety behavior, observability or
 deterministic replay.
 Rollback target and previous known-good artifact are recorded before promotion.

outcomes
Execution

Learning quality

rate
Do not collapse these into a single reward function unless a future design proves that doing so
preserves the hard safety constraints. Multi-objective evaluation with explicit constraints is safer and
more interpretable.
10. Determinism and reproducibility contract
 UTC event time plus monotonic sequence/correlation IDs.
 
 Immutable raw evidence references; derived features never replace source evidence.

 Code SHA, dependency/environment fingerprint, config hash and schema version.
 
 Dataset/version identifiers and exact inclusion/exclusion windows.
 
 Persisted random seeds for Monte Carlo or stochastic inference.
 
 Idempotent evaluators: reprocessing the same event must not create contradictory labels.
 
 Append-only corrections: never silently rewrite prior evidence; supersede with explicit lineage.
 
 Clock/freshness semantics are explicit and testable.
 
 All learned artifacts have provenance: evidence set -> hypothesis -> experiment -> candidate -> promotion.

13. Acceptance tests for the future system
 Given a KillSwitch event ID, an operator can reconstruct exactly which condition, data, code and config caused
 the trigger.
 The same event can be replayed offline and reproduces the same protective decision.
 
 A post-event favorable price move cannot automatically relabel a safety-correct trigger as wrong.
 
 A stale incident can be attributed to venue, network, clock, parser or local processing where evidence permits;
 UNKNOWN remains valid when it does not.
 Bull/Bear and Dynamic-Scope transitions are traceable to trusted input snapshots and reason codes.
 
 Every proposed threshold/model/policy change links back to the incidents/evidence that motivated it.
 
 No candidate can alter live behavior without passing the defined validation/promotion path.
 
 Old and new behavior can be compared on exactly the same evidence pack.
 
 Rejected hypotheses/candidates remain auditable.
 
 A rollback restores a known-good, versioned artifact without ambiguity.
 
14. Explicit anti-patterns
 Unsafe online adaptation: 'KillSwitch fired too often, therefore increase threshold immediately.'
 
 PnL-only labeling: treating a profitable counterfactual as proof that a safety block was wrong.
 
 Hindsight leakage: evaluating the original decision using information unavailable at decision time.
 
 Data-quality conflation: teaching Bull/Bear logic from stale or untrusted observations.
 
 Silent mutation: changing configs/model weights without a versioned candidate and promotion record.
 
 Single-score optimization: allowing economic reward to compensate for a safety regression.
 
 Untraceable AI judgment: accepting a model conclusion without persisted inputs, version, rationale/evidence
 references and deterministic surrounding policy.
15. Future handover / resume protocol
When this PDF is reintroduced in a later Peak_Trade chat, use it as a design target, not as evidence that
implementation already exists. The first task must be a read-only current-state delta analysis against the
then-current Master Runbook and repository.
RESUME REQUEST 1. Read current canonical Master Runbook / relevant repository surfaces. 2. Treat this
PDF as AUTHORITY=NONE future design intent. 3. Produce CURRENT_STATE vs BLUEPRINT delta matrix. 4.
Identify earliest safe implementation slice. 5. Do not mutate runtime, risk, strategy, config or docs
without explicit Owner GO. 6. Preserve existing Safety Authority and promotion gates. 7. HARD STOP
after adjudication unless the Owner authorizes implementation.
16. North-star architecture
MARKET / ACCOUNT / EXECUTION / DATA-QUALITY EVIDENCE | v CANONICAL SNAPSHOTS | v MARKET/PRICE STATE
-> TRADING / EXECUTION LOGIC -> DECISION EVENT | | | +--> Risk/Safety Authority | | | +--> Kill /
Stale / Block v Controlled Productive Path | v Runtime Outcome Evidence | v Attribution +
Counterfactual Evaluation | v Learning / Hypothesis Layer | v Research -> Validation -> Robustness ->
Promotion Gates | v Versioned Candidate Release RULE: Learning can propose. Validation can prove.
Governance can promote. Runtime Safety remains independently authoritative.
North-star statement: Peak_Trade should become a system that learns from every consequential
decision while remaining able to explain, reproduce and audit why that decision happened. The
learning mechanism improves future candidates; it never retroactively changes evidence and never
acquires implicit authority to bypass safety.
